creator: macro-economy
topic: The dollar's share of global reserves has been falling for twenty years. Almost everything said about why is wrong.
title: "The number" asks for a level over a window; a share, index or ratio is a composite and nothing asks what it is made of
expected: Phase 1's first row, and the matching column, should ask what the metric is constructed from — numerator, denominator, scope, whether the reported population changed mid-series — and whether the observed movement can originate anywhere other than the behaviour being explained. For a reserve-currency share that means separating valuation effects from flows, or stating explicitly that the notebook cannot.
got: RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:24-25 asks 'What is it now, what was the extreme, over what period? Get the dates.' dimensions.ts:26-27 restates it as 'What the price actually did, and over what window.' Answered exactly as written on this topic it yields '71% to 58%, 2001-2025' — a figure roughly half of which is exchange-rate revaluation, not de-dollarisation. The nearest thing in the methodic is Phase 2 tension shape 5, 'the category error — the subject is being measured with the wrong instrument' (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:49), but that is a tension-FINDING shape that fires only if you already suspected it, not a Phase 1 breadth obligation. Worse, the column's emptyMeans ('No measured baseline — every claim downstream is unanchored') implies the converse: that a FULL number column means downstream claims ARE anchored. For a composite metric a full column certifies an artefact.
l2_priority: Run Phase 1 on this topic verbatim and record whether the executor spontaneously decomposes valuation from flow WITHOUT being asked. L1 reads prompts charitably; this is exactly the gap the SKILL warns about. If an Opus run does it unprompted, downgrade to minor and re-target at dimensions only. If it does not, the notebook will be complete by every quality-bar row and fail the senior bar.

title: No source-primacy tier on facts, and no quality-bar row requiring a primary series for load-bearing quantitative claims
expected: facts[] should carry a primacy tier (primary | secondary | aggregator | vendor) orthogonal to confidence, and the quality bar should require load-bearing quantitative facts to reach primary or carry a named research_gaps entry. The MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED contract that already governs the craft library (knowledge/README.md:36-41) is the obvious model and is not applied to notebook facts.
got: facts[] carries only confidence: high|medium|low with a free-text reason (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:45-46); the only primacy rule is 'vendor research is low by default'. 'high' is available to a newspaper's paraphrase of a public series. Phase 9 (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:112) asks the researcher to DECLARE aggregator use in research_gaps — disclosure, not requirement — and the quality bar (:119-130) has no primacy row. The reference run declares exactly this failure and ships anyway (notebook.json:430, NOTES.md:51-54).
l2_priority: Count, in a live run, how many load-bearing facts reach a primary series unprompted. RECURRENCE NOTE: the Bitcoin run's own NOTES.md:79 proposed this exact edit against the RESEARCH-PROMPT quality bar and it was not adopted — per rubric.md this outranks impact arithmetic.

creator: macro-economy
topic: The dollar's share of global reserves has been falling for twenty years. Almost everything said about why is wrong.
title: A researcher-computed quantity has no home — it is demoted into `conclusions` or forced to invent a source
expected: A derivations[] class (or a fact subtype) carrying inputs, method, result and a reproducibility note, ranked as EVIDENCE. A valuation/flow decomposition computed from IMF COFER plus BIS FX indices is more checkable than any aggregator-sourced fact in the reference notebook and should rank above one.
got: Two homes, both wrong. facts[] requires a source (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:94 — 'Every fact dated and sourced. No exceptions') and the 'No prose' rule (:92) forbids the two lines of method that make a computation auditable — so even writing source: 'own calculation' loses the only thing that makes it verifiable. conclusions.ts:11-24 defines the alternative tier as explicitly sourceless REASONING, OFF by default, rendered to the user as what the model inferred. The ladder therefore demotes DERIVED material — the opposite direction from the usual interpretive-evidence complaint, and more damaging, because derived material is the most reproducible content a notebook can hold.
l2_priority: In a live run, attempt to record a computed decomposition and see where it lands. If it is written as a fact with source 'own calculation', check whether any downstream render or reviewer can tell it apart from a sourced observation — that indistinguishability is the actual harm.

title: The counter-case has a hardcoded polarity and inverts for any topic whose verdict is the null hypothesis
expected: Phase 1's counter-case row phrased relative to the verdict — 'the strongest argument against the answer this notebook is heading toward' — so it points the same way as Phase 6's steel-man regardless of which side the verdict lands on. The board column needs the same neutrality, or two sub-groups.
got: Phase 1 row 6 asks for 'the strongest argument that nothing unusual is happening' (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:32). Phase 6 asks for 'the strongest case against your own verdict' (:88-90). These coincide only when the verdict is 'something unusual IS happening', which is the shape of the single topic the methodic was derived from. This topic's verdict is the null ('the decline is valuation and small-sleeve diversification, not de-dollarisation'), so Phase 1 row 6 points at the notebook's OWN thesis while Phase 6 points at de-dollarisation. dimensions.ts:36-37 collapses both into one column whose label matches Phase 1 and whose emptyMeans cites Phase 6, so a reviewer cannot tell which polarity a card in that column has.
l2_priority: Run a null-verdict topic and check whether counter-case and steel_man end up holding the same material (the collapse) or opposite material filed under one label (the confusion). Likely convergence with any other Creator whose topic is a debunk.

title: The researcher's own prior is never recorded and the verdict is never tested against it
expected: A Phase 0 that records the researcher's stated prior before searching, and a check at Phase 2/6 asking whether the verdict is a discovery or the prior returned with citations. A notebook field (prior / researcher_position) so the check is auditable later.
got: Phase 2 compares 'what people believe' against 'what the evidence shows' (RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:37-38) with no notion of WHOSE belief; tension.expectation (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:34) inherits the same anonymity. The only treatment of an author's prior as a hazard anywhere in the methodic is ENGINES.md:91-92, D-honest tell 2 ('Can any candidate actually win against the author's prior?') — scoped to executing one engine, not to conducting research, and absent from the prompt, the schema and the quality bar. On a topic whose contrarian take has become its niche's consensus, a run returns the researcher's own position with citations attached and passes every quality-bar row.
l2_priority: Declare the prior BEFORE the run, then check whether the produced verdict contradicts it anywhere. If the notebook simply restates the prior with sources, that is the finding in its produced form. artifact_check is present-but-missed because the concept exists at ENGINES.md:91 — but promoting it out of one engine's honesty section into a research obligation is a prompt edit, not a discoverability fix.

creator: macro-economy
topic: The dollar's share of global reserves has been falling for twenty years. Almost everything said about why is wrong.
title: `currency` models staleness but not revision; `as_of` cannot express a data vintage
expected: as_of should distinguish the period a figure describes from the release/vintage it was read at, and currency should carry a revisable flag with advice ('this series is back-revised; state the vintage or use a ratio'). Official statistics — COFER, BEA, Eurostat, BLS, national accounts — are routinely revised backwards after publication.
got: facts[].as_of is a single date (NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md:47) and currency models only forward decay: half_life, expires_first, durable, advice (:84-86, RESEARCH-PROMPT.md:108-110). The failure mode it cannot express is a fact that does not expire but silently CHANGES — a script citing a superseded vintage is not stale, it is wrong, and it re-dates itself as current because as_of still looks recent. The reference topic (a spot price) has no revision concept, which is why the schema has none.
l2_priority: Check whether a live run on an official-statistics topic records which release it read. Convergence expected with any Creator working from government or IMF/BIS data.
